judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital is a mechanical list of principal amounts (which do sum to the $147,485,000 on the cover) but it creates two labels — 'Series 2004 Bonds' and 'Series 2004 Auction Bonds' — for the same instruments with the loose phrase 'being sometimes referred to together herein', leaving unclear when each label controls. That double-labelling is the only textual softness; the rest is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.3(f) (c007) then deems 'Bonds or Auction Bonds' to refer to each series of both defined sets, which compounds rather than resolves the recital's dual naming, and the recital names the Issuer as the New Mexico Hospital Equipment Loan Council while the notice block in 5.3 (c034) addresses the Issuer as Hospital Services Corporation. That is a genuine recital-versus-operative mismatch, though a minor one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line recital that BD 'is to perform certain duties set forth herein'; 'certain duties' is indefinite but the recital expressly defers to the operative text for content. There is nothing to construe on its own face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It points to Sections 2.3-2.6, which do specify BD's duties, so recital and operative text align; the only friction is that 2.3(b) (c017) adds a purposive parenthetical about the lowest possible interest rate that this recital does not foreshadow. That friction lives in 2.3(b), not here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital is doubly hedged ('except as provided therein', 'except as otherwise provided therein') and contains an OCR-level date slip ('May I, 2004'), but its substance — the Auction Rate is what the Auction Agent determines results from the Auction Procedures — is definite. The layered exceptions push the real rule out into the Indenture rather than making this text ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with 2.1(a) (c009), which assigns the Auction Agent the same rate-determining role, and with 2.1(b)'s incorporation of the Auction Procedures. No conflicting operative provision was found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A factual recital of appointment and of the Company's direction under Section 2.6(a) of the Auction Agreement; the only wobble is the OCR 'bas been appointed'. Nothing in the words admits two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It recites that the Company procured this agreement, which sits awkwardly with 5.5 (c036) denying any Person other than the Auction Agent, Bond Insurer and BD a right or claim under it even though the Company is a signatory. That is a recital-versus-operative tension, but the sharp edge is in 5.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single clause stating that the Auction Procedures require one or more Broker-Dealers; it is definite and purely introductory. Nothing to name as ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.1(c) (c011), which contemplates other Persons executing Broker-Dealer Agreements. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deeming rule turns 'purchase', 'sale' and 'holding' into beneficial ownership interests 'unless the context clearly requires otherwise', a self-referential escape hatch whose boundary a court would have to draw. That saving phrase is the named soft term, though the drafting is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with 2.5(b)'s (c025) rules about who remains the Broker-Dealer on transfers and with 2.6(a)'s (c027) delivery mechanics, both of which assume beneficial-interest trading; no contradiction surfaced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any reference herein to Bonds or Auction Bonds shall be deemed to be references to each series of Series 2004 Bonds and Series 2004 Auction Bonds' collapses two defined terms that the recital already treats as coextensive, so its operative effect is uncertain. The second sentence's 'apply separately to each series' pulls the other way from the first sentence's aggregation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against recital c001, which says the Series 2004 Bonds are 'sometimes' called the Series 2004 Auction Bonds, this deeming clause leaves genuinely unclear whether a series-specific obligation (e.g. the fee formula in 2.5(b)) is computed per series or in aggregate. That is a modest whole-instrument coherence point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard due-authorisation and enforceability warranty with the usual 'assuming the due authorization, execution and delivery' qualifier; every term is a term of art. Nothing here carries two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It assumes due execution only 'by the Auction Agent' although the Company is also a signatory party to this three-party agreement, a small gap rather than a conflict; nothing in Sections 2-5 contradicts the warranty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision defines 'Auction' by reference to each periodic implementation of the Auction Procedures and is definite except that 'Initial Periods' is not defined here. The sentence structure is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the Auction Procedures incorporated by 2.1(b) (c010) and matches recital c003's description of the Auction Rate; no inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A blanket incorporation of 'all of the provisions' of the Auction Procedures and Settlement Procedures 'in their entirety' without identifying the document or edition from which they come — the reach of the incorporation is exactly the kind of thing courts construe. The absence of any conflict-of-terms rule between the incorporated material and the body text is a real defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls in an unbounded body of external terms while 5.4 (c035) declares this agreement plus the issuance documents to be the entire agreement and 3.1(b) (c030) limits the Auction Agent to duties 'expressly set forth herein, or expressly incorporated herein by reference pursuant to Section 2.1(b)'. Harmonising incorporation-in-entirety with the express-duties-only limit is not obvious.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'BD agrees to handle customer orders in accordance with its respective duties under applicable securities laws and rules' imports an undefined external standard into a contractual promise, and 'the obligations of, and limitations and restrictions placed upon, a Broker-Dealer' is stated without saying where those obligations are found. Both phrases invite argument about whether regulatory duties become contract duties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines Broker-Dealer status by 'the definition ... contained in the Indenture', whereas 2.5(b) (c025) refers to the definition 'contained in the Series 2004 Auction Bonds' — the same concept sourced to two different documents. That mismatch is a specific internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision permits Broker-Dealers to bid for their own accounts, then lets the Company prohibit that by notice, then carves out affiliates — the interplay of permission, prohibition power and 'Notwithstanding the foregoing' leaves the default rule about own-account support bidding open to competing readings. 'Participate in Auctions for their own accounts' is not bounded by any standard of purpose or disclosure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 2.3(b) (c017), which frames BD's role as implementing Auctions to achieve 'the lowest possible interest rate', an unrestricted right to bid for its own account is in tension with that stated purpose, and 5.5 (c036) would deny the Company a remedy even though this clause gives the Company the prohibition power. That is a genuine whole-instrument strain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed deadline and two named items to be communicated; 'other electronic communication acceptable to the parties' is the only soft phrase and it is a common formulation. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the first line of the 2.3(a) (c016) timetable exactly ('By 9:30 a.m.'), so it is internally consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The confidentiality undertaking is qualified by 'except as otherwise required by law' and then by a three-item proviso whose limb (c) — disclosure whenever failure 'would expose the Auction Agent to loss, liability, claim, damage or expense' — is a catch-all wide enough to swallow the undertaking. 'Believes are Existing Owners' also states a subjective standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The permitted disclosees (Trustee, Issuer, Company, BD) sit consistently with 3.1(a)'s (c029) statement that the Auction Agent acts solely as agent of the Trustee; no contradictory provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As of the opening of business on such date' is ambiguous as between the Auction Date and the preceding Business Day on which notice is given, and its placement after 'Series 2004 Auction Bonds' leaves the modifier dangling. That is a small but nameable defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 3:00 p.m. cut-off matches 2.3(d)'s (c019) 3:00 p.m. cut-off for BD notices, so the timing regime is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause fixes a schedule, then allows the Auction Agent to change it 'at any time' at the Company's direction to reflect 'then currently accepted market practices', then overrides with the BMA Recommendation 'unless the Auction Agent is instructed otherwise' without saying by whom — three separate open-textured hooks. The BMA sentence also states an 11:30 a.m. Submission Deadline that displaces the 1:00 p.m. deadline in the table without saying what happens on a daily Auction Period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2.4(b) (c021) separately requires notice of schedule changes without a deadline, duplicating and partly undercutting the notice timing built into this clause. The interaction is untidy rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical '(and thereby achieving the lowest possible interest rate on the Series 2004 Auction Bonds)' can be read as a mere statement of purpose or as an affirmative performance standard binding BD, and the duty to 'contact Potential Owners' has no defined scope or intensity. Those are precisely the words two parties would read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The stated purpose of the lowest possible rate is hard to reconcile with 2.1(d) (c012), which lets BD bid in Auctions for its own account, and with 5.5 (c036), which would leave the Company — the party bearing the interest cost — without a claim under the agreement. Both make this a live whole-instrument issue.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The no-netting rule and the separate-Order requirement are stated crisply; 'substantially in the form' and 'reasonably acceptable' are conventional softeners. Nothing genuinely two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the Exhibit B order form referenced here and the Settlement Procedures incorporated by 2.1(b); no conflicting provision found.
